topics.title: The Holy Spirit - Who the Holy Spirit | The Significance of the Holy Spirit Primary 5/Basic 5 Term 2 Week 3 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES
RELIGIOUS STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 3
PRIMARY 5
THEME - THE HOLY SPIRIT WORKING IN US
PREVIOUS LESSON - The Meaning of Pentecost | The Event of the Pentecost | The Spiritual Significance of the Pentecost Primary 5/Basic 5 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - THE HOLY SPIRIT
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Who the Holy Spirit is?
3. The Holy Spirit is the third Person in God’s Head
4. The Significance of the Holy Spirit
5. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain who the Holy Spirit is.
2. identify the Holy spirit as the third Person in God’s head.
3. state the significance of the Holy Spirit.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can narrate the event of the pentecost.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of The Bible
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Holy Spirit is the the spirit person promised by Jesus Christ to his true believers to guide.
John 16 : 8
The work of the Holy Spirit is to convict us of our sin. And when He has come, He will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
9 of sin, because they do not believe in Me.
WHO THE HOLY SPIRIT IS?
Holy Spirit is the the spirit person promised by Jesus Christ to his true believers to guide, comfort and counsel.
John 16:8 New King James Version (NKJV)
The work of the Holy Spirit is to convict us of our sin. And when He has come, He will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
THE HOLY SPIRIT IS THE THIRD PERSON IN GOD’S HEAD
Reading Matthew 28:19
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit…
The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Trinity, mainly defined as:
“There is one God, eternally existent in three persons -
the Father,
the Son, and
the Holy Spirit.”
LESSON 2 - THE PURPOSE OF THE COMING OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
The purpose of the coming of the Holy Spirit is -
1. To fulfil the promise of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2. To comfort us.
3. To teaches us how to pray.
4. To inspire us.
5. To discerns the false spirits.
6. To reveals the will of God.
THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
The importance of the Holy Spirit are -
1. He guides us into Jesus truth.
2. He directs our steps.
3. He gives spiritual gifts.
4. He gives us power to preach the gospel.
5. He gives us the assurance of heave.
REVISION AND WEEK LESSON ASSESSMENT
As stated in performance objectives or lesson evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Asks pupils to narrate the event of the day of pentecost.
Pupil’s Activities - Summary the event of the day of pentecost.
3. Uses pupil’s responses to introduce and discuss who the Holy Spirit is.
Pupil’s Activities - Pay attention to the lesson introduction to participate actively the discussion.
4. Tells pupils about the Holy Spirit is the third person in God.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and state the Holy Spirit is the third person in God.
5. Explains the significance of the Holy Spirit.
Pupil’s Activities - Analyze the significance of the Holy Spirit and explain.
6. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the summary of the lesson and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - The Meaning of Pentecost | The Event of the Pentecost | The Spiritual Significance of the Pentecost Primary 5/Basic 5 Christian Religious Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Asks pupils to:
1. explain who the Holy Spirit is.
2. identify the Holy spirit as the third Person in God’s head.
3. state 5 significance of the Holy Spirit.

topics.title: God Creates: Meaning of Creation, Things Created by God, and the Creation of Man in God’s Own Image | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 1 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
GOD CREATES: MEANING OF CREATION, THINGS CREATED BY GOD AND THE CREATION OF MAN IN GOD’S OWN IMAGE
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 1
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - First Term, Second Term and Third Term Christian Religious Studies (CRS) Plan Lesson Notes and Scheme of Work for Primary 4 (Basic 4)
TOPIC - GOD CREATES
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Creation and Things Created by God
3. Creation of Man and Man Created in God’s Own Image
4. Importance of God’s Creation
5. Weekly Assessment
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of creation.
2. Mention things created by God.
3. Explain how God created man.
4. Explain what it means that man was created in God’s image.
5. State the importance of God’s creation.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned about God as the Creator and some of the things He created.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by helping pupils understand creation in greater detail and the special position of human beings in God’s creation.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Pictures of God’s creation
3. Charts showing living and non-living things
4. Flashcards
5. Pictures of human beings, plants and animals
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. All Relevant Materials
6. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God is the Creator of the heavens, the earth and everything in them. He created both living and non-living things and made human beings in His own image and likeness.
When we look around us, we see many wonderful things such as plants, animals, rivers, mountains, the sun, moon and stars. These things remind us of God’s power, wisdom and greatness.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of creation, things created by God, how God created man, and what it means that man was created in God’s own image.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF CREATION
Creation is the act of bringing something into existence. God is the Creator of all things because He made the heavens, the earth and everything in them.
The Bible teaches that God created the world and everything in it. God’s creation shows His power, wisdom and greatness.
Bible References: Genesis 1:1-31; Genesis 2:1-3.
THINGS CREATED BY GOD
God created many things, including living and non-living things.
Examples of Living Things
- Human beings
- Animals
- Birds
- Fish
- Plants
- Trees
Examples of Non-Living Things
- Sun
- Moon
- Stars
- Land
- Water
- Mountains
- Rivers
All these things are part of God’s creation.
LESSON 2 - THE CREATION OF MAN
God created man on the sixth day of creation. He created human beings as male and female and gave them the responsibility to care for His creation.
According to Genesis 1:26-28, God said that He would make man in His image and likeness. God blessed human beings and gave them responsibility over other creatures.
The creation of man was special because human beings were created in God’s image and likeness.
MAN CREATED IN GOD’S OWN IMAGE
The Bible teaches that God created man in His own image and likeness.
Being created in God’s image does not mean that human beings look exactly like God. It means that human beings have special qualities and abilities that reflect God’s character and enable them to relate with Him and with others.
Being created in God’s image teaches us to:
- Respect human life.
- Love and care for others.
- Do what is right.
- Show kindness and compassion.
- Care for God’s creation.
- Treat everyone with dignity and respect.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF GOD’S CREATION
God’s creation is important because it:
1. Shows God’s power and wisdom.
2. Provides what human beings need to live.
3. Helps us appreciate and worship God.
4. Teaches us to care for the environment.
5. Provides food and other useful resources.
6. Reminds us to respect all human beings.
7. Helps us understand the greatness of God.
Lesson: God created the heavens, the earth and everything in them. Human beings were created in God’s image and given the responsibility to care for His creation.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What is creation?
A. The act of bringing something into existence
B. The act of destroying everything
C. The act of buying something
D. The act of hiding something
2. Who created the heavens and the earth?
A. Moses
B. Abraham
C. God
D. David
3. Which of these is a living thing created by God?
A. Stone
B. Animal
C. Moon
D. Mountain
4. On which day did God create man?
A. First day
B. Third day
C. Fifth day
D. Sixth day
5. In whose image did God create man?
A. Moses’ image
B. Adam’s image
C. God’s image
D. Abraham’s image
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. God is the ______ of all things.
7. Creation means bringing something into ______.
8. God created man on the ______ day.
9. God created man in His own ______ and likeness.
10. Human beings should ______ for God’s creation.
C. True or False
11. God created the heavens and the earth.
12. Plants and animals are part of God’s creation.
13. Human beings were created in the image and likeness of God.
14. Human beings should destroy God’s creation.
15. God’s creation shows His power and wisdom.
D. Matching
16. Creation - A. A living thing created by God
17. God - B. The act of bringing something into existence
18. Man - C. The Creator of all things
19. Animal - D. Created in God’s image and likeness
20. Environment - E. The natural surroundings in which living things exist
ANSWER KEY
1. A 2. C 3. B 4. D 5. C
6. Creator 7. existence 8. sixth 9. image 10. care
11. True 12. True 13. True 14. False 15. True
16. Creation - B. The act of bringing something into existence
17. God - C. The Creator of all things
18. Man - D. Created in God’s image and likeness
19. Animal - A. A living thing created by God
20. Environment - E. The natural surroundings in which living things exist
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that creation is the act of bringing something into existence and that God is the Creator of the heavens, the earth and everything in them. God created living and non-living things such as human beings, animals, plants, the sun, moon, stars, land and water.
Pupils also learned that God created man on the sixth day in His own image and likeness. This gives human beings special value and teaches us to love, respect and care for one another and to take good care of God’s creation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What is creation?
- Who created the world?
- Mention some things you see around you that God created.
- Why should we care for God’s creation?
The teacher explains that God is the Creator of the world and everything in it.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention things created by God.
Step 2: Meaning of Creation
The teacher explains that creation is the act of bringing something into existence, God created the heavens, the earth and everything in them and refers pupils to Genesis 1:1 and explains that God is the Creator of all things.
Pupils’ Activities:
Pupils explain the meaning of creation in their own words and read the Bible passage.
Step 3: Things Created by God
The teacher explains that God created both living and non-living things and gives examples such as:
- Human beings
- Animals
- Birds
- Fish
- Plants
- Sun, moon and stars
- Land and water
- Mountains and rivers
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention other things created by God and classify them as living or non-living things.
Step 4: The Creation of Man
The teacher explains that God created man on the sixth day. God created human beings as male and female and gave them responsibility to care for His creation and refers pupils to Genesis 1:26-28 and explains that the creation of man was special.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen, read the Bible passage and answer questions about the creation of man.
Step 5: Man Created in God’s Own Image
The teacher explains that God created man in His own image and likeness, and that this does not mean that human beings look exactly like God, but that they have special qualities and abilities that reflect God’s character.
The teacher also explains that being created in God’s image teaches us to:
- Respect human life.
- Love and care for others.
- Do what is right.
- Show kindness.
- Care for God’s creation.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain what it means to be created in God’s image and mention ways they can show love and respect to others.
Step 6: Importance of God’s Creation
The teacher explains that God’s creation:
- Shows God’s power and wisdom.
- Provides what human beings need.
- Helps us appreciate God.
- Teaches us to care for the environment.
- Reminds us to respect human beings.
- Provides useful resources for life.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the importance of God’s creation and explain ways of caring for it.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of creation.
- Group 2: Mention five things created by God.
- Group 3: Explain how God created man.
- Group 4: Explain what it means that man was created in God’s image.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the meaning of creation, things created by God, the creation of man, what it means to be created in God’s image, and the importance of caring for God’s creation. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework, or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
God Creates and Wants Us to Be Creative: Meaning of Creativity, Things Made by Man, and Creation as a Sign of God’s Love | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 2 Christian Religious Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. What is creation?
2. Mention five things created by God.
3. On which day did God create man?
4. What does it mean that man was created in God’s image?
5. State three reasons why we should care for God’s creation.
